And if you could look at the second paragraph of that page. What is indicated there about the use of special ballots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's indicated that the non-Serbs, those who do not declare themselves as Serbs, will have yellow ballot papers to be distinguished from the other ballot papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how were they making this distinction according to the instructions? Upon what type of documentation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's said that citizens shall vote at the polls where they are registered, and the excerpts from the general electoral register. Citizens who have not been registered in the electoral register shall be allowed to vote after having displayed their identity cards.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you would please look at the ballot paper and the wording at the top and ballot paper, and the wording at the bottom. I would ask if this exhibit is consistent with the information you received and the analysis that you performed as part of your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer Prosecution Exhibit 25 for Identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, in your report at paragraphs 131 to 132, you discuss the events in Prijedor and you discuss the role of propaganda in the events in Prijedor. And in that regard I would like to provide the witness with what has been marked Prosecution Exhibit 26 for Identification, noting that this exhibit is part of the report, but for ease of discussion it has been re-produced as an exhibit. Dr. Greve, is this a quote that appears in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a quote that appears in my report. It's taken from the British historian, Noel Malcolm, and his book, "Bosnia, A Short History." And it gives in a very small format the essence of my findings for the area of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you could very succinctly summarise for the Trial Chamber what you believe to be the significance of this quotation mark or this quotation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it has --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANN
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think on your feet, please, Mr. Vann, if you want to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANN
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. The exhibit speaks for itself, and it would be improper to have the witness comment on the significance thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I rather agree. Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would offer that into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time we would ask that the witness be provided -- what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 27 for Identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, could you tell us what this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the United Nations document. It's circulated by the Secretary-General of the United Nations, and distributed to and through the General Assembly and the Security Council. It is attached to the covering letter. There is a report made by Mr. Tadeusz Mazowiecki, who was the Special Rapporteur of the Commission on Human Rights, and he was particularly looking at the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you will turn to page 10, as those pages are numbered on the top of the document, paragraphs 38 to 43, beginning on page 10. And that section deals with what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It deals with media in areas controlled by de facto Bosnian Serbs authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you look at paragraph 40 of that section, what is indicated there about --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same objection. We don't object to this document being admitted, but the document is so comprehensive and deals with a report on all media in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Are there any other paragraphs you wish to draw to our attention, Ms. Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that would be paragraph 41, as it deals with television from Belgrade. And as to paragraph 40, involving television in Pale and Banja Luka, and ethnic terminology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer the exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would next ask that the witness be provided with what has been marked -- what we would ask to be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 28 for Identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this exhibit is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a translation of an article in the newspaper, Kozarski Vjesnik. It's dated June 17, 1994, and it's headlined, "The Green Berets 'Attack'".

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look at pages 23 and 24, what is the significance of the discussion on those pages, beginning with "I concluded," in relation to propaganda in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is indicated in these paragraphs that the so-called Green Berets, or those who are referred to in the headline as Green Berets, the Muslims, have attacked, which is in quotation marks. It is the Serb in charge of the SDS in Ljubija, which is a town in Opstina Prijedor, in the Municipality of Prijedor. He is explaining how he is disarming the Territorial Defence unit, "resorted to cunning," as he is saying, it has not been an attack or a battle. He is suggesting there is an attack, and that way he is calling upon everyone of the non-Serbs to come to defend Ljubija. And as they do not come to defend Ljubija, all weapons are confiscated or taken under his control and his people's control.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We offer that into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 28.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, I would now like to turn to a general topic dealing with cooperation between civilian authorities, police, and the army in the area which you reviewed and analysed for purposes of your report. And in that regard I would like to provide you with what I would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 29 for Identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is yet another newspaper article, again Kozarski Vjesnik, dated 30th of July, 1993, headlined under, "Loot of public property." It's a report by a man named Bogdan Delic, who is the new head of the public security station, the police station, in short, not exactly. The precise translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we stipulate to admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, if you would just describe it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And there are just two or three areas I would like to emphasise with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Judge Greve, if you would look to the bottom -- to the bottom of the first page, just above the caption, "Keraterm, emptied overnight." And if you could indicate there the suggestion about the strong bond between the various bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here it is suggested that the main political bodies, police and the army, all are working closely to together.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And at the bottom of that page, the last sentence, carrying over --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't see this text here where this inference is being drawn. And if Dr. Greve would kindly point it out, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise for not having done that. It's the last sentence before the new headline, subhead line, "Keraterm emptied overnight." And it reads, "All of this suggests the existence of a strong body between parts of the known political bodies, police, armies, Serb Democratic Party and local authorities." End of quote.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then looking at "Keraterm emptied overnight," there is an -- what is the indication there about the cooperation of various bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, it's suggested that the police, the army, the authorities are working closely together. I should, perhaps, say that as the name "Keraterm" will be used within another context. Also, "Keraterm" here is used as a storage room.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And going back a bit to when you were discussing the population in the various ethnic groups in the Prijedor Municipality, the first sentence there indicates how many people used to live within the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Including then the first sentence starting, "After Keraterm emptied overnight, about 50,000 people of other ethnic origins used to live within the territory of this municipality."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the commentator goes on to indicate what is the total value of their property estimated as?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, again, it's the report of the head of the Public Security Station quoted, and his same line as I stopped the previous quote, "The total of their property has been unofficially estimated at several billion Deutschmarks. A smaller proportion of that property was destroyed during the military operations, but most of it was saved."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would offer that into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 29. In that regard, that is, dealing with cooperation, I would ask that the witness be shown what has been marked Prosecution Exhibit 30 for identification. And what is that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik, dated 20th of May, 1994, headline, "We know our goal." It's an interview with Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja, commander of the 43rd Prijedor motorised brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you would please look at the second full paragraph, beginning with "Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja." And if you would look about halfway down that paragraph, where you see the sentence beginning "Yugo crisis." The line under that, what does Colonel Zeljaja indicate concerning the action regarding Territorial Defence weapons or units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is suggesting or he is informing that the weaponry that used to belong, the weaponry and technical equipment that were at the disposal of the Territorial Defence, was actually taken under the control of the Serb leadership and the Serb military. He is stating and I am moving -- it's actually the end of a sentence, "Yugo Crisis." But I am one, two, three, four -- five lines further down. And the final part of the sentence reads, "And place them under our control in our depots."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to the third page of that exhibit, with the paragraph beginning, "Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja," what does the colonel say about the linkage with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is suggesting that it's immediately linked to the leadership of the SDS, the Serb democratic party, giving them important support --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: --- (Kindly be advised microphone is not activated)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I must insist that if you're going to object, you must do so formerly. Don't, please, conduct an informal conversation with the witness. Now, what is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. It was just so that the Defence could follow the presentation of the evidence. Dr. Greve, would you mind pointing to the text that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I must insist, you must do it through the bench if you have a point to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence could not follow the presentation of the evidence in the reading. Could you kindly instruct the witness to point out to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let us find out precisely. I haven't followed it either. Start again on this point, would you, Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I apologise for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again, if we would turn to the third page of the document, and the first full paragraph beginning, "Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja, it is true." And then, if you would look at, please, at the next few lines that follow, what does Colonel Zeljaja indicate about the linkage with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is suggesting that they are closely linked. And starting in the middle of that line, he is saying, the brigade command was, because of that, immediately linked to the leadership of the SDS, Serb Democratic Party, giving them important support as they do for all decent Serbs to organise themselves for self-defence in case of an attack by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And again, if we could turn to the fourth page. And if we could look again in the first full paragraph, beginning, "Colonel Radmilo Zeljaja." Looking at the language that is four lines up from the bottom of that paragraph, with the line that begins, "Region." Could you tell us what is indicated there about cooperation between various units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Starting almost in the middle of that line, he is saying, "Everyone knows the very close cooperation between the army and the police." And it's also suggesting -- it was stating, I continue where I stopped, "Such cooperation was also established with the leaders of the party, the people in power, the crisis staff and all decent Serbs who were and still are of importance for this town."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, if I may direct you back to the third page, beginning at the very bottom of that page, the second line up, with the words, "Our command started work." Could you tell us what is said about setting up two different headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's stated, in short, that the Muslims and the Croats were also present in the headquarters. And therefore, I am quoting from mid -- last line. "Therefore, I was forced to set up two headquarters in that command." "One" -- I am continuing the quotation on the next page -- "One was small and more senior, where most of the decisions were made and the other was more fictitious."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would offer that into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 30. I would ask at this time that the witness be provided what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 31 for identification. Dr. Greve, in the exhibit that was just admitted, there was discussion about the Territorial Defence and the fact that that was taken over. And, now, in this exhibit, could you please tell us what this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also a newspaper article taken from Kozarski Vjesnik, 13th of May, 1994. Staff changes in RPC, the information and business centre, Kozarski Vjesnik, manager Slobodan Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would stipulate to the submission of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then we would simply, Your Honour, move to the bottom of the exhibit, with the paragraph beginning, "Kuruzovic was one." And if you would look at the last sentence, what does it indicate concerning positions that Slobodan Kuruzovic had held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It stated that he was also the commander of the Serb Territorial Defence headquarters in Prijedor and one of the organisers of defence in power in Prijedor on the night between 29th and 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer that into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to object based on your previous orders when scheduling this trial. You have indicated that the expert witness shall testify through his or her report. And exactly the content of this has been mentioned on the various points in the report to Dr. Greve. And unless we are going to go and be testifying on direct, basically in the process of introducing the documents, we are going to allow expert witness to testify again in direct, I don't object. But if there is going to be available to the Prosecution, I hope that you are going to accord the same latitude to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can point out the significance of the document. There can be no objection to that. And, of course, the Defence can cross-examine on them. Again, there can be no objection to that. You may want to cross-examine, I notice, on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not think -- I don't think that you, basically, you know, perceived the import of my point. Where I am going, I am going back to your order that was made in March, that you ordered that the expert witnesses shall testify on the case in chief for the party that is calling them in writing in their report. And we have heard that Judge Greve, an expert for the Prosecution, shall briefly testify to introduce certain documents. And if the Defence stipulates to the documents being admitted and documents having been discussed in the report, this presents either violation of your orders or second bites to the apple. And if it's a second bite to the apple, we merely suggest that we would like to receive the same privilege when we present our case in chief, if that becomes necessary. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll consider it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Hollis, I see it's ten past five. Can we get through this witness in chief now?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe so. We have several additional exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe so. We have several additional exhibits for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see if we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided, what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 32 for identification. Dr. Greve what is this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik, 19th November 1993. It is headlined, "21st November, the day of the Security Services of Republika of Srpska. The Joy and the Sorrow of the Blue Angels." The "Blue Angles" refers to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would stipulate to admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Greve, if you would look at the first page of the document, the third paragraph of that beginning, "In the preparations undertaken." And if you would look at the next sentence, please. What type of cooperation is being discussed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in close cooperation between the Serb army and the Serb police station. And quoting the sentence starting on the third line, "All the preparations had been carried out in an exemplary cooperation with the Serb army and in very short time, 13 illegal Serb police stations with 1,600 officers had been formed, while the SDA was still in power in Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you would go down, please, two lines, beginning with the language, "it was decided” to the end of that paragraph. What type of cooperation and coordination is being discussed there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to get to the feet on this document. Just, in all due respect, to Judge Greve because there was discussion in the opening statements about the translation. And the word "illegal" here has just been used with the -- out of context, completely prejudicial. The original document does not have that meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll have that checked. We will mark that. And, in due course, we can have it checked as to the exact meaning. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, if we look -- would you please, because I am lost, I confess. Could you please repeat your answer to my question about what type of cooperation is being dealt with in those last few lines of that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's paragraph 3 and it's the last few lines, which is referring to agreement and cooperation between the Serb army, the Serb Democratic Party and the Executive Committee of the Municipality of Prijedor to seize power from the Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, what is indicated about the Prijedor seizure of power? By whom is it indicated that that was done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's stated that due to outstanding organisation and discipline, the Serb police in Prijedor seized power without a shot being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you will look to the bottom of that document, what is indicated there about reception centres being set up? That would be two lines from the top, beginning with "Following."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's stated that following the old uprising, reception centres were set up in Keraterm, Omarska and Trnopolje. The offices of the SJB police station, it's stated in brackets, we're taking people in for questioning and carrying out operative processing and security operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now we're on the second page of that document. And what is indicated in that next paragraph, the first line about cooperation between police in various locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's suggested that or stated that the police in the nearby districts or municipalities are working together with the police from Prijedor to take care of non-Serb groups labelled as extremist groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer that document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to the term "cleansed" in quotation marks in the last paragraph of that document because quotation marks, to the best of my recollection, and I can't see the original that well. It's not very legible. I can't see them there. So it seems that quotation marks are not -- cleansing here is a term that is questionable. It's not an original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, we will have that checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In that document that you were just discussing, they indicated the take-over of power in Prijedor and also indicated about the camps. In your report at paragraphs 157 to 204 and paragraphs 337 to 505, you discuss the take-over of Prijedor and the camps that were established. I would ask at this time that the witness be provided with what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 33 for identification. Could you tell us what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is, again, a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik, dated 9th April 1993. It is an interview with the late Simo Drljaca, Deputy Minister of the Interior of the Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And could you please look at the first paragraph of that document, beginning "The man who was selected." And look at the second sentence and what is indicated there about illegal work and armed men in police stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, without, perhaps putting significance to the word "illegal," I don't know if it's correctly translated, I have related to the translation as is. But he is stating that as a parallel structure, at least, a force of 1.775 well-armed men in 13 police stations were ready to carry out the difficult tasks in the times ahead. That is, to take over power in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And concerning the take-over of power, what is indicated there about that take-over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It stated that it was successfully executed in half an hour without, again, a single bullet fired. It's the second time that's stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you would look at the paragraph directly above, "A great task was executed." What is indicated there about informative talks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's stated that more than 6.000 informative talks were held at the gathering centres of Omarska Keraterm and Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And regarding the information concerning the parallel structure, the take-over and the informative talks, is this consistent with your analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is. And this document was also available to me prior to making my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: You've reviewed this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer Prosecution Exhibit 33. At this time, I would ask that the witness be shown what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 34, for identification. And can you tell us what this is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is also a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik, 6th of August, 1993, it relates to the third anniversary of the Serb Democratic Party of Prijedor. And it's headlined, "Preventing a Repetition of the Serb Massacre of 1941."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who is the person who is the subject of this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Mr. Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how is he introduced in the article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Chairman of the SDS District Committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you will look at the next paragraph, could you tell us what he indicates about the SDS arming of people in Prijedor? And if you would look at the last sentence of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is stating that it was needed for the Serbs to continue to arm themselves. Excuse me, it's stated in the last sentence in this paragraph that the SDS leadership saw what they, meaning the Muslims and the Croats were planning, and started to arm their own people in order to prevent a tragedy of 1941.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, what does Mr. Miskovic say about the take-over of power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is again stating, confirming the date and stating there was not a single shot fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what does he indicate about forming the army and police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is stating that they quickly, "they" meaning the Serbs in this context, quickly formed their army and their police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again, is this information consistent with your analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And we will offer Prosecution Exhibit 34. Dr. Greve, in your report you discuss camps, and among those, you discuss the camp at Trnopolje. At this time, I would ask that you be shown what we have marked as Prosecution Exhibit 35 for identification. And I would ask that first you tell us what the general area that is depicted by this map is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map is the map of the Municipality of Prijedor. Not all of it, but the central part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And if you could put that map on the overhead, please. If you could, perhaps, point to where the Trnopolje area is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Trnopolje area is close to what looks like a lake. It's an artificial fish farm or fish pond. It's actually listed on the map as the station of Kozarac. It's not stated Trnopolje, but it's Trnopolje station or the station of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And based on your information and analysis, is this the area where the Trnopolje camp was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And is there any significance to that area in terms of lines of communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's located next to the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the railway station goes where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The railway station comes from up here, from Prijedor. It crosses through the Trnopolje or the station of Kozarac. It continues then to Omarska and goes all the way to Banja Luka-Duboj. It goes further. So it's actually the railroad linking Zagreb and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And for reference on the map, this is a larger fish pond, that's in blue there. And in about the top third of that is where you find Kozarac, that is marked as Kozarac, the rail station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to point at it on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And for points of reference, you mentioned earlier that it goes, the railway line goes to Prijedor, could you show us on the map where the Prijedor town is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We may just follow the railroad going west, north-west and we come to the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We would offer that as Prosecution Exhibit 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: In your report you also discuss the deportations or the transfer of people from Prijedor outside the municipality. In that regard I would like to ask the witness to review what we would ask be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 36 for Identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Hollis, it's coming onto half past five, so it may be convenient, after we've dealt with this exhibit, to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a communication to the press, which is submitted by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It is from their headquarters in Geneva. And it is headlined, "ICRC --", the International Committee of the Red Cross, "-- evacuates 1,560 people from Trnopolje Camp," it's dated 2nd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you will look at the second line of the substance of that article. When does it indicate that this evacuation occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It occurred a day before the 1st of October that same year.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you will look at the second paragraph of that article. What does it indicate about the first time the ICRC was able to enter Trnopolje Camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's stating that they only were able to enter this camp for the first time on the 10th of August, that very year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, what do they indicate about an agreement concerning this evacuation of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is stated that the evacuation is under the terms of the agreement reached already the year before in London.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We offer this as Prosecution Exhibit 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that will be a convenient moment. We'll adjourn now until half past nine tomorrow morning.
